_readme: VERIFICATION REGISTRY. A behaviour change whose proof needs a story run gets an entry here in the same push (pre-push gate scripts/admin/check-verify-coupling.js; escape: a `Verify: none (<reason>)` or `Verify: <entry-id>` commit trailer). After ANY validation run: `node scripts/admin/verify-run.js <storyId> [--env=prod] --write` judges every pending entry against that stored run and prints CONFIRMED / FAILED / HUMAN / NOT COVERED. A run is evidence only for commits its recorded build (stories.data.analytics.build.commitFull) contains; an absent run shape (no over-the-shoulder page, no iterate repair ...) is NOT COVERED, never a pass. Fields: id; title; commits (every one must be in the run's build); addedAt; claim (what a new run must show, one sentence); runShape (all must hold: any | full-story | trial | age-band:N (or N|M) | needs-shot:<shot> | needs-iterate-repair | needs-char-fix | needs-inpaint | needs-fresh-idea | needs-worn-off | needs-fresh-avatar-sheet | needs-composite — defined in scripts/admin/verify-checks.js SHAPES); check ({kind:'auto', fn} names a function in verify-checks.js, {kind:'human', what} says what to look at); status (pending | confirmed | failed | superseded); evidence[] (appended by verify-run.js --write or --mark; never edited by hand, never deleted). An auto FAILED stays pending and is printed loudly; only a human --mark sets failed. Entries are never deleted: a change that is replaced becomes superseded with a note.

entries.title: The aerial shot is allowed, never owed; the camera-position total is unchanged
entries.claim: The page planner's prompt names no aerial floor and the plan counters raise no SHOT_AERIAL_COUNT, while the book still carries its camera-position pages.

entries.title: Unrequested lettering on a page becomes a rendered_text finding in code
entries.claim: Every evaluated scene version stores letteringInventory {items, declared} (what the check compared), and readable writing the page did not declare is stored on that version as a rendered_text finding with source lettering-check: overlay, misspelled or misplaced-legible CRITICAL quoting the text, misplaced scribble MINOR, a fitting correctly spelled sign silent.

entries.title: sceneIntent no longer ends on a verbless mood tag (the sentence that became a painted caption)
entries.claim: No brief ends sceneIntent on a sentence carrying mood/atmosphere/tension/standoff/feeling: the rule now asks for setting and light only (measured baseline 36/177 = 20%).

entries.title: Emotion is one enum on both sides, compared in code
entries.claim: At least 90% of brief characters[] rows carry an emotion from the closed list, emotion-check findings appear with code-set severity, and every CRITICAL one is a real opposite-tone face (human look: false-CRITICAL risk).

entries.title: The arc panel's SENSE lens: anything a reader would stop at is a fault
entries.claim: The arc panel runs with the SENSE lens and its faults name turns the arc's own facts contradict (a lost thing its size would find at once, an avoidable danger); human read of the panel output.

entries.title: Sizes and looks leave the arc and the plan; the prose makes no size comparison
entries.claim: The final arc, the page plan and the page text contain no size comparison ('as big as', 'the size of', '-sized', 'so gross wie', compound '-gross' ...); run 6 had several in each.

entries.title: A Visual Bible description states no scale; page-side readers add it via withScaleNote
entries.claim: No newly authored Visual Bible animal description contains a SCALE_PHRASES string (run 6: 'stands knee-high to an adult' etc. in every animal).

entries.title: An ultra-wide page on a shared vantage gets a derived plate pulled back to a size, and the page records it
entries.claim: Every ultra-wide page sharing a vantage carries plateDerivedFor 'ultra-wide', its emptyScenePrompt carries the sized pull-back, and the plate image is visibly pulled far back from the base plate of the same place (human look).

entries.title: Over-the-shoulder: the near figure is a crop with the camera behind it, never on a contact page
entries.claim: Every over-the-shoulder page gives its near figure perspective over-the-shoulder, the built image prompt carries the crop directive, the near figure touches nothing (no hands:true interaction), and the image shows the camera behind a cropped head and shoulder with the subject small and deep (human look).
entries.backlog: tasks/BACKLOG.md 'Verification pending' — over-the-shoulder / ultra-wide line (OTS accepted as is by the owner 2026-09-23; subject-size idea untried)

entries.title: A generated idea reaches the story as prose, never a labelled 'Satz 1 — setup' list
entries.claim: The stored idea (idea_original / idea_used) of a run started from a generated idea carries no 'Satz N —' / slot label.

entries.title: An iterate rewrite's characters[] is the cast; parent VB citations are carried
entries.claim: Every iterate version's sceneCharacters is a subset of its rewritten brief's characters[] (run 6 p17 drew four absent boys' reference cards).

entries.title: The char-fix prompt carries the finding's type as a fixed phrase, never the judge's sentence
entries.claim: No char-fix version prompt contains an 'Issues to fix:' judge sentence; defects appear only as 'Defect to fix:' fixed phrases.

entries.title: A garment off by design is never charged as missing: the entity grid reads the page's worn state
entries.claim: Every page where a character's garment is 'off' appears in that character's '--off:<id>' entity grid, never in the wearing grid.

entries.title: The text diff pass sees the findings the repair answered and invents no sentence
entries.claim: The stored diff prompt carries 'FINDINGS THE REWRITE ANSWERED' per page, and no applied diff correction introduces a sentence neither BEFORE nor AFTER had (human read of any the measure flags).

entries.title: One style rulebook for every prose pass; blind STYLE audit; motive at the act; ending on the act; the repair may decline
entries.claim: The blind audit files FAULT[STYLE] lines, the repair analysis names any finding it declines, and the final text has no bare narration fragments, no paired negations and ends on a concrete act (human read of the counts the check lists).

entries.title: One helper says WHO a fix is about; no cast name or age/gender fallback reaches the image model
entries.claim: No inpaint instruction names a cast character or uses 'the N-year-old male/female figure'; figures are identified by age noun, garment and position.

evidence.note: 7 inpaint instruction(s), no cast name, no fallback descriptor; outside this entry, a creature NAME reached Grok: p13 v1 Turi

entries.title: No image-model repair text names a figure the model has no reference for: inpaint, char-fix pose lines, manual repair route
entries.claim: No inpaint instruction names a Visual Bible animal or secondary character; no char-fix prompt names a bible figure (nor, where the record names the target, another cast member); no manual-repair payload names a cast member or bible figure. Such figures are identified by kind, colouring/garment and position.

entries.claim: Every multi-face emotion scene_fix names no cast character and gives each clause both a remove and a show half; the repainted faces show the declared beat (human look).

entries.title: Every cover is briefed the way a page is: Art Director Scene prose + REQUIRED OBJECTS, no KEY STORY ELEMENTS
entries.claim: Superseded 2026-09-24 by covers-are-pages: the full-story cover hint (and its Scene line) is gone — a full-story cover is a page the Art Director briefs from its cover beat; the trial cover keeps its own builder.

entries.title: A full-story cover is a page: the Art Director briefs it from a code-written cover beat; it renders, is evaluated and repairs through the page path
entries.claim: On a new full story every cover record is briefedAsPage with an Art Director brief (prose + METADATA) and its PLAN line, every figure looksAt the viewer, the textPosition is the beat's copy space, the sent prompt carries no KEY STORY ELEMENTS and no METADATA, and no cover_failed / beats_cover_brief_missing event is logged.

entries.title: No kept re-plan round raises the cast/focal must-fix count; round 1 faces the guard too
entries.claim: A full story's kept round 1 ends with no more cast/focal must-fix findings than the first check (stable measure), or the round is under discardedRounds with a 'raised the cast/focal must-fix count' reason.

entries.title: A story started from generated ideas records which card the customer picked
entries.claim: A run started from a generated idea stores stories.data.ideaPick and an idea_picked row in idea_events (staging now; production only after migration 039 is applied there).

entries.title: Readers wait on the progress screen until the story is complete; hour message; bar moves with time
entries.claim: Starting a story on staging shows the hour message prominently, then as a small note under the spinner; the modal stays (no partial book, no stage text) until the job completes and then opens the finished story; the bar is near the server percent (about 57% when the text is done) and never drops at the end.

check.what: Start a story on staging as a NON-dev account (or dev mode off): first ~7 s a large panel says the story takes about an hour and an email follows; then it shrinks to a small line under the spinner and tips/avatars rotate. The modal must not close when the first image exists; after completion the reader lands on the finished story. Nav % and My Stories card show only a percentage and never go backwards near the end.

entries.title: Idea cards show only the final idea text, never [DRAFT]/[REVIEW] scratch
entries.claim: Generating ideas on staging leaves each card in its loading state until the final idea text appears in one piece; no [DRAFT] or [REVIEW] text ever shows in the box.

check.what: In the wizard story step, click generate ideas and watch both cards: spinner/progress until a clean idea appears at once; no text streaming in, no [DRAFT]/[REVIEW] words.

entries.title: A reader who left the wizard keeps tracking a story past 60 minutes
entries.claim: After leaving the wizard, the nav % and the My Stories generating card keep tracking a story that runs longer than 60 minutes, and the story opens (Ready badge / auto-open) on completion.

check.what: Start a story on staging, click Continue in Background, browse elsewhere; return after 60+ minutes: the nav % button and the My Stories generating card are still there and advancing; on completion the Ready badge appears and opens the finished story.

entries.title: The entity grid judge returns only types from its closed list
entries.claim: Every entity finding stored in finalChecksReport.entity carries a type from evalBuckets.ENTITY_CHECK_TYPES (baseline before the change: 6.5% off-list on staging, 7.5% on production); an off-list one is logged as a parse error and never routed to a repair.
